scenes.goal: Establish the invocation to the Unborn Lord and the teaching that grace alone empowers the surrendered soul.

turn.text: In the very same way, Your grace empowers those who surrender to You. Remove my sins, sorrows, and destitution—this alone is my prayer.

scenes.goal: Portray Bankatlal's restless longing, fruitless search, and the pivotal meeting with Ramajipant who affirms Maharaj as a Yogi.

turn.text: He said to Bankatlal, 'I have heard your account. The great soul you describe to me must surely be a Yogi.'

scenes.goal: Show Govindbuwa's kirtan at the Shiva temple, Bankatlal meeting Pitambar, and their discovery of Maharaj behind the temple.

turn.text: As the two walked toward the Kirtan, they suddenly spotted Samarth sitting on the stone pavement at the back of the temple.

scenes.goal: Depict the Tumba water miracle at the shallow stream, Pitambar's doubt, and his realization of Maharaj's divine power.

turn.text: Then a miracle occurred! Wherever he placed the gourd, a deep hollow formed in the stream bed and the gourd submerged completely.

scenes.goal: Show the betel nut offering, coin refusal, Maharaj's teaching on devotion over material, and his sending devotees to the kirtan.

turn.text: 'Because you possessed that devotion, I met you again. Reflect upon this in your heart, and you will understand.'

scenes.goal: Present the kirtan discourse, Maharaj completing the verse, Govindbuwa's recognition, Maharaj's refusal to move, and his teaching on consistency of word and deed.

turn.text: 'Do not be a mere belly-filling preacher on this earth. Go, complete your Kirtan; I am listening from here.'

scenes.goal: Show kirtan ending, Bankatlal's joy, father's permission, meeting Maharaj at Manik Chowk at sunset, and bringing him home.

turn.text: Thereafter, on the fourth day at sunset, Sadgurunath met Bankatlal at Manik Chowk.

scenes.goal: Depict Maharaj's welcome at Bankatlal's home, the Pradosh worship, food dilemma, serving afternoon puris, massive meal, overnight stay, and elaborate mangal snan.

turn.text: He consumed nearly three seers of food and stayed right there for the entire night.

scenes.goal: Show adornments, naivedya, house becoming Dwarka on Monday, Ichharam's unresolved wish, his fast, bath, and worship of Maharaj.

turn.text: Bankatlal's house truly became Dwarka! That day happened to be Monday, the sacred day of Lord Shiva.

scenes.goal: Portray Ichharam's lavish feast, Maharaj's self-dialogue and consumption, the vomiting leela, Ramdas parallel, and the teaching on insistence yielding adverse results.

turn.text: He vomited forcefully, expelling the food. A similar incident was once enacted by Sri Ramdas.

scenes.goal: Show cleanup after vomiting, reseating Maharaj, darshan by crowds, arrival of dindi troupes, bhajan, and Maharaj's continuous 'Gan Gan' chant giving him the name Gajanan.

turn.text: Meanwhile, Maharaj on his seat chanted from his lips under the guise of bhajan: 'Gan Gan Ganat Bote'.

scenes.goal: Convey philosophical reflections on name/form, bliss, Shegaon as pilgrimage center, author's humility, Maharaj's unpredictable routine, and closing invitation with phalashruti.

turn.text: Now, keep devotion to listen to the next chapter. Do not delay in seizing this spiritual opportunity!
